newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares fall, property rally fizzles out.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares fall, property rally fizzles out.

text.p: Singapore shares plummeted at midday break on Monday as fears of another U.S. interest rate hike overshadowed a milder-than expected public housing loan curbs announced over the weekend.
"Wall Street plunged almost 150 points last Friday. The Americans are almost certain the Fed will raise interest rates soon. The question is how much," said one dealer.
The Straits Times Industrials Index dived 21.48 to 2,047.00 Market volume was 80 million shares with 304 falls and 21 rises.
Dealers said there was uncertainty over the impact of new public housing loans measures on the private property sector.
The new rules include a limit of two subsidised loans to Singaporeans buying public housing.

"Prices of resale (public housing) flats are likely to fall. Prices of lower-end private properties may also fall to encourage upgrading. There won't be much recovery in property stocks," a dealer said.
The property index gave back most of its gains, up just 0.34 point to 682.53, after touching a high of 699.72 in early trade.
SembCorp, Cycle & Carriage and foreign shares of DBS and UOB fell. Property firms Wing Tai and DBS Land were off their highs.
